{"name": "run_python", "arguments": {"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Convert revenue from string to float, stripping commas
# First, ensure all revenue strings are properly formatted
# Check for commas
print('Revenue strings with commas:', df['revenue'].str.contains(',', regex=False).sum())

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Drop QA orders (if any)
# The documentation says there are 6 QA orders with revenue 999999.99
qa_mask = (df['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99)
print('QA orders found:', qa_mask.sum())

# Drop refunded orders
refunded_mask = (df['status'] == 'refunded')
print('Refunded orders:', refunded_mask.sum())

# Apply filters: keep only completed orders, remove QA and refunded
# Final population: completed orders, non-QA
filtered_df = df[~qa_mask & ~refunded_mask]

# Now compute conversion rate by customer_segment
conversion_rates = filtered_df.groupby('customer_segment')['converted'].mean() * 100

# Find the segment with highest conversion rate
highest_segment = conversion_rates.idxmax()
highest_rate = conversion_rates.max()

print(f'Conversion rates by segment:\n{conversion_rates}')
print(f'Highest segment: {highest_segment} ({highest_rate:.2f}%)')}}
